parts.text: Run a one-question senior behavioral interview about conflict. Use this as my answer to the question: I disagreed with a PM who wanted a full launch to meet a partner deadline. I was responsible for launch reliability, so I proposed a staged rollout. I aligned two engineering teams and the PM on actual checkout-error and latency thresholds. The first stage caught a checkout regression before broad release, so we fixed it without exposing the remaining users. I learned to turn stakeholder disagreement into an explicit, measurable risk decision early. Score only what I said, give feedback, and finish the one-question session.

Feedback uses the complete behavioral rubric with evidence for every score.
Behavioral feedback identifies missing impact evidence without inventing example quantities.
The agent configures, selects, records feedback, and only then completes the session.

parts.text: Run one easy arrays question. For the repeated-alert-window problem, my attempt is: scan left to right, store each key's latest index in a map, and return the first key where i - lastIndex <= k; otherwise update the index. This is O(n) time and O(n) space. Review this by inspection, score it, and finish the session.
